L787: ### 5.2. CSS Parsing Results
L788: 
L789: The result of parsing can be any of the following (or lists of these):
L790: 
L791: stylesheet
L792: 
L793: 
L794: A stylesheet has a list of cite238†rules .
L795: 
L796: rule
L797: 
L798: 
L799: A cite238†rule is either an cite107†at-rule or a cite106†qualified rule .
L800: cite107†at-rule L801:     An cite107†at-rule has a name which is a cite239†string†infra.spec.whatwg.org , a prelude consisting of a list of cite240†component values . cite241†Block at-rules (ending in a {}-block) will additionally have a list of cite242†declarations and a list of child cite238†rules . (cite243†Statement at-rules , ending in a semicolon, will not.)
L802: qualified rule
L803:     A qualified rule has a prelude consisting of a list of component values, a list of declarations, and a list of child rules.
L804: Note: Most qualified rules will be style rules, where the prelude is a selector cite244†[selectors-4] and its declarations are cite245†properties .
L805: 
L806: declaration
L807:     A declaration has a name which is a cite239†string†infra.spec.whatwg.org , a value consisting of a list of cite240†component values , and an `important` flag which is initially unset. It also has an optional `original text` which is a string (captured for only a few declarations).
L808: Declarations are further categorized as property declarations or descriptor declarations, with the former setting CSS cite245†properties and appearing most often in cite106†qualified rules and the latter setting CSS cite246†descriptors , which appear only in cite107†at-rules . (This categorization does not occur at the Syntax level; instead, it is a product of where the declaration appears, and is defined by the respective specifications defining the given rule.)
L809: component value
L810:     A component value is one of the cite247†preserved tokens , a cite248†function , or a cite249†simple block .
L811: preserved tokens
L812:     Any token produced by the tokenizer except for cite155†<function-token> s, cite131†<{-token> s, cite195†<(-token> s, and cite203†<[-token> s.
L813: 
L814: Note: The non-cite247†preserved tokens listed above are always consumed into higher-level objects, either functions or simple blocks, and so never appear in any parser output themselves.
L815: Note: The tokens cite132†<}-token> s, cite196†<)-token> s, cite208†<]-token> , cite221†<bad-string-token> , and cite218†<bad-url-token> are always parse errors, but they are preserved in the token stream by this specification to allow other specs, such as Media Queries, to define more fine-grained error-handling than just dropping an entire declaration or block.
L816: function
L817:     A function has a name and a value consisting of a list of cite240†component values .
L818: simple block
L819: {}-block
L820: []-block
L821: ()-block
L822:     A simple block has an associated token (either a cite203†<[-token> , cite195†<(-token> , or cite131†<{-token> ) and a value consisting of a list of component values.
L823: 
L824: cite250†{}-block , cite251†[]-block , and cite252†()-block refer specifically to a cite249†simple block with that corresponding associated token.

L826: Tests
L827:   * cite253†parse-invalid-input.html†wpt.fyi cite254†(live test)†wpt.live cite255†(source)†github.com L828: ### 5.3. Token Streams
L829: 
L830: A token stream is a cite256†struct†infra.spec.whatwg.org representing a stream of cite257†tokens and/or cite240†component values . It has the following cite258†items†infra.spec.whatwg.org :
L831: 
L832: tokens
L833: 
L834: 
L835: A cite259†list†infra.spec.whatwg.org of cite257†tokens and/or cite240†component values .
L836: Note: This specification assumes, for simplicity, that the input stream has been fully tokenized before parsing begins. However, the parsing algorithms only use one token of "lookahead", so in practice tokenization and parsing can be done in lockstep.
L837: 
L838: index
L839: 
L840: 
L841: An index into the cite257†tokens , representing the progress of parsing. It starts at 0 initially.
L842: Note: Aside from cite260†marking , the cite261†index never goes backwards. Thus the already-processed prefix of cite257†tokens can be eagerly discarded as it’s processed.
L843: 
L844: marked indexes
L845: 
L846: 
L847: A cite262†stack†infra.spec.whatwg.org of index values, representing points that the parser might return to. It starts empty initially.
L848: CSS has a small number of places that require referencing the precise text that was parsed for a declaration’s value (not just what tokens were produced from that text). This is not explicitly described in the algorithmic structure here, but the cite237†token stream must, thus, have the ability to reproduce the original text of declarations on demand. See cite263†consume a declaration for details on when this is required.
L849: 
L850: Several operations can be performed on a cite237†token stream :
L851: 
L852: next token
L853: The item of cite257†tokens at cite261†index .
L854: 
L855: If that index would be out-of-bounds past the end of the list, it’s instead an cite153†<eof-token> .
L856: 
L857: empty
L858: 
L859: 
L860: A token stream is cite264†empty if the cite265†next token is an cite153†<eof-token> .
L861: 
L862: consume a token
L863: 
L864: 
L865: Let `token` be the cite265†next token . Increment cite261†index , then return `token`.
L866: 
L867: discard a token
L868: 
L869: 
L870: If the cite237†token stream is not cite264†empty , increment cite261†index .
L871: 
L872: mark
L873: 
L874: 
L875: Append cite261†index to cite266†marked indexes .
L876: 
L877: restore a mark
L878: cite267†Pop†infra.spec.whatwg.org from cite266†marked indexes , and set cite261†index to the popped value.
L879: 
L880: discard a mark
L881: 
L882: 
L883: cite267†Pop†infra.spec.whatwg.org from cite266†marked indexes , and do nothing with the popped value.
L884: 
L885: discard whitespace
L886: 
L887: 
L888: While the cite265†next token is a cite166†<whitespace-token> , cite268†discard a token .
L889: 
L890: process
L891: To cite269†process , given a following list of token types and associated actions, perform the action associated with the cite265†next token . Repeat until one of the actions returns something, then return that.
L892: 
L893: An cite153†<eof-token> is a conceptual token, not actually produced by the tokenizer, used to indicate that the cite237†token stream has been exhausted.
L894: ### 5.4. Parser Entry Points
L895: 
L896: The algorithms defined in this section produce high-level CSS objects from lists of CSS tokens.
L897: 
L898: The algorithms here operate on a token stream as input, but for convenience can also be invoked with a number of other value types.
L899: 
L900: To normalize into a token stream a given `input`:
L901: 
L902:   1. If `input` is already a cite237†token stream , return it.
L903:   2. If `input` is a list of CSS cite257†tokens and/or cite240†component values , create a new cite237†token stream with `input` as its tokens, and return it.
L904: 
L905:   3. If `input` is a cite239†string†infra.spec.whatwg.org , then cite147†filter code points from `input`, cite270†tokenize the result, and return the stream of tokens.
